s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: CD1A positivity and osteolytic lesions are characteristic

shortlist.label: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of skin and bone, with potential for other systems

shortlist.label: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of disseminated papules and histiocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histiocytic infiltrate with kidney-shaped nuclei, though less common in children

shortlist.label: Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Differential for histiocytic disorders without clear Langerhans cell involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of osteolytic lesions, subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive staining for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining are characteristic of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis. The disease primarily affects the scalp and bone, which aligns with the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: While the patient has osteolytic lesions, there is no evidence of multisystem involvement, such as liver or spleen enlargement, which is typical of Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The histological findings and positive CD1A staining do not support Juvenile Xanthogranuloma, which typically presents with Touton giant cells and lacks CD1A positivity.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histological findings do not match Rosai-Dorfman Disease, which typically presents with lymphadenopathy and emperipolesis on histology.

rejected.label: Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: The positive CD1A staining and presence of kidney-shaped nuclei are characteristic of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, making Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis an unlikely diagnosis.
